messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER - Sev=P1 - model-routing failures detected in us-west-2. >500 errors spiking on chat endpoints since 12:03 UTC. Paging oncall.
 tj (oncall): I’m on it. Seeing 5xx rates ~21% for /v1/chat/completions in us-west-2. Alerting SRE. reproducible in prod and canary A.
 maria (sre): quick triage: logs show a lot of `incompatible_request_schema` from the runtime. Example: `error: unexpected field 'messages' for model 'gpt-instruct-v2'` — looks like chat-format payloads routed to an instruct-style variant.
 tj (oncall): timeline: 11:58 UTC config push to routing-policies service (small change unrelated), 12:00 UTC we started seeing increased fallback activity. Could the routing policy change have incorrectly pinned a variant?
 lee (eng-runtime): digging into route resolution. I see a pinned entry for `customer-route:acme-chat` pinned to `gpt-instruct-v2@rev7` in us-west-2. That’s wrong — chat clients expect streaming + messages array. Instruct models expect `prompt` string -> schema mismatch -> 500 on our side.
 helena (support): AcmeCorp support ticket: "/chat is returning 500 since 12:04 UTC. We rolled back client changes, still failing." They flagged production impact for their webchat feature.
 tj (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) remove mistaken pin OR 2) set override to route to a compatible chat variant while we investigate. Which is faster?
 maria (sre): Option 2 (override) is less risky if we need to preserve the pin for some customer-specific reason. But current pin appears accidental. I can remove the pin if ops approves.
 lee (eng-runtime): I can apply a routing override now to prefer `gpt-chat-v2` for the affected route in us-west-2. Command: 
```
# temporary routing override
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/routing/overrides \ 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \ 
 -d '{"route":"acme-chat","region":"us-west-2","preferred_variant":"gpt-chat-v2"}'
```
 tj (oncall): @lee do it. Also capture the pin id so we can revert if needed.
 lee (eng-runtime): applied override at 12:18 UTC. Confirming: error rate dropped to ~1.2% in the next minute. Metrics: median latency steady. Rolling error budget still hit for the minute window but customer requests are succeeding now.
 maria (sre): I removed the wrong pin from routing-policies at 12:22 UTC: `pin_id=pin-3421` (was pinned to gpt-instruct-v2). Change logged in audit: `routing-policies.edit by maria`.
 helena (support): Told AcmeCorp at 12:24 UTC that we applied a fix and to confirm. They responded: "chat restored, thanks". Marking as customer-impacting, partial disruption for ~20 minutes.
 sam (product): How did a pin end up with an incompatible variant? We need guardrails so product or SRE can't accidentally pin instruct on chat routes.
 tj (oncall): Root-cause hypothesis: a manual pin command mistakenly referenced the wrong `variant` identifier for a rollout. Also config push at 11:58 had a permissive merge that accepted pins without validating interface compatibility.
 lee (eng-runtime): Action items (short): 1) add validation in control-plane to reject pin requests that are interface-incompatible (chat vs instruct vs embeddings) — low-risk. 2) Add warning on Console when pinning shows mismatch. 3) Add an automated canary test that sends chat payloads after pin changes to detect 5xxs. I'll file PRs.
 maria (sre): Ops mitigations: add a fast alert rule for `incompatible_request_schema` rate > 1% for >2m to page earlier. Also add runbook step: check for pinned variants if chat endpoints spike.
 helena (support): Customer followup: provide incident timeline + link to postmortem once available. AcmeCorp wants assurance this won't recur.
 sam (product): I'll prep a cross-team RFC for pin validation and Console UX changes. Also propose we add a small pre-flight check in the pin API to simulate one request shape.
 tj (oncall): Handoff: I’m wrapping up. Next oncall @alex will monitor. Leaving follow-ups: jira INC-4523 (postmortem), TASK-987 pin-validation, SRE alert tuning. Last seen healthy at 12:35 UTC.
 maria (sre): Confirming last_message: system stabilized, fallback loop stopped after removal + override. We will run a postmortem and include exact timelines and customers affected.
 oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - Sev=P1 -> mitigated. Postmortem required. Incident closed for now; reopen if we see regression.
